newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian voter support up for Hanson - poll.
newsitem.headline: Australian voter support up for Hanson - poll.

text.p: Maverick Australian politician Pauline Hanson's newly-formed One Nation party has the same voter support as the Australian Democrats minority party, according to a newspaper poll published on Wednesday.

The Australian newspaper said the poll results showed it was possible that Hanson's party could win seats in the states of Queensland and New South Wales in the upper house Senate, if Prime Minister John Howard called a double dissolution election.
The prime minister has the constitutional option of calling an early nation election, dissolving both houses of parliament, if the Senate rejects a piece of legislation three times.
"But the party would have little chance of winning Senate seats in a half-Senate election, giving Mr Howard added incentive to run full-term," the newspaper said.
The poll found that 18 percent of voters would support minor parties or Independents, the highest percentage since the last election on March 2, 1996.
It said four percent of those voters would vote for Hanson's One Nation party, while four percent would also vote for the Democrats, two percent for the Greens and eight percent for "others".
"Immediately before the launch of the party (on April 11), only one percent of voters nominated Pauline Hanson," the newspaper said.
The increase came at the expense of Howard's Liberal-National coalition (down two points) and the Democrats (down one point).
Political analyst Malcolm Mackerras said the poll results confirmed his view that Howard would not go to an election before December 1998.

"Pauline Hanson will be re-elected as the Member for Oxley, but no other candidates from her party will be elected in either house of parliament -- that's my considered view," Mackerras was quoted as saying.
Hanson sparked a bitter race debate last year with her anti-Aborigines and anti-Asian comments.
She has also been linked to a newly-released book containing unsubstantiated claims that Aborigines were once cannibals who ate their children.
